guide.description: tee <file> writes its stdin to a file AND passes it straight through as stdout — unlike >, which sends output only to the file and shows you nothing. That makes tee useful mid-pipeline: you can save an intermediate result to disk while still piping it into the next command. Like >>, tee -a appends instead of overwriting.

flags.desc: append to the file instead of overwriting it

examples.note: prints hi AND writes it to out.txt
copy.log gets the full file, wc -l still counts lines from the same stream

exercises.title: See it and save it
exercises.task: Grep for admin rows in users.csv and pipe the result into tee, saving it to admins-new.csv while also printing it.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: grep admin users.csv finds the right rows, same as the redirect lesson
Pipe that into tee admins-new.csv instead of using >

criteria.label: Output is printed to the terminal

exercises.title: Append with -a
exercises.task: admins.csv already has ada's and alan's rows. Grep for grace's row and pipe it into tee -a admins.csv to append it WITHOUT losing what's already there.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: Plain tee would overwrite admins.csv and lose the existing rows — use -a

criteria.label: admins.csv keeps ada and alan, and now has grace too

exercises.title: tee mid-pipeline
exercises.task: Pipe the full contents of access.log through tee, saving a copy to full.log, then continue the pipeline into wc -l to count its lines.

access.log.content:
200 GET /home
404 GET /missing
200 GET /about
500 GET /api/users
200 GET /home
404 GET /old-page

hints: tee sits in the MIDDLE of the pipe: cmd | tee <file> | next-cmd

criteria.label: wc -l still sees the full stream and counts 6
full.log has a copy of the whole file
